items.titleJa: 【エラー対応】TypeScriptの「Uint8Array is not assignable to BufferSource」の原因と解決方法
items.summaryJa: TypeScript 5.9.3 で、Push API の applicationServerKey に Uint8Array を渡す際に、戻り値の型を Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> と明示することで型エラーが解消しました。原因は、Uint8Array を省略して書くと Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike> となり、適合する BufferSource の型と合わないためです。結論として、戻り値の型を Uint8Array<ArrayBuffer> にするか、文字列のまま渡す方法もあるが、本文では前者の修正を推奨しています。

items.summary: はじめに margin-inline-startとmargin-left、なんとなく使い分けていないだろうか？ 自分はそうだった。 padding-block-startのようなプロパティを、雰囲気で書いていた。 「この方向に余白を足す」という感覚で手が動くだけで、なぜ物理プロパティではなく論理プロパティを選んだのか、聞かれたら答えられなかった。 動くコードは書けても、選んだ理由を説明できない。これはまずいと思い、ちゃんと調べてみることにした。 まだ実務経験も浅く、ベテランエンジニアからすれば当たり前の話かもしれない。それでも、同じように「なんとなく」で書いてしまっている人の参考にな...
items.titleJa: CSS論理プロパティ、"なんとなく" から卒業する
items.summaryJa: 論理プロパティは、書字方向に基づく配置になるため、横書き日本語・英語では左を指す物理プロパティと異なる動作をする。縦書きやRTLなど書字方向が変わる環境では、論理プロパティを使うことで表示崩れを防げるが、4値のmarginショートハンドは現状物理プロパティとしてしか解釈されない点に留意が必要だ。結論として、実務では一貫性を重視し、Flex/Gridではgapを使い、それ以外は一方向のmarginに統一するなどの運用基準を持つべきだとしている。

items.title: Why GitHub now ships more CSS, not less
items.summary: 🚀 Frontend Focus #​760 — September 30, 2026 | Read on the web Improving Site Performance by Shipping More CSS — GitHub details how it spent three years purging styled-components and 'CSS-in-JS' from github․com in favor of CSS Modules. The result? Shipping more CSS, but GitHub reports 55% less time to server-side render a page. Josh Black and Marie Lucca (GitHub) 💡 CSS Modules isn't a browser feature or standard, but a widely supported bundler convention where classes in a .module.css file get rewritten to unique names, scoping styles per file with no runtime cost. Reports That Time Out Aren't a Frontend Bug — The report worked in testing. In production, it scans months of rows and times out before it renders. That's not a frontend bug, it's the query behind it. TimescaleDB extends Postgres so that query returns fast at scale. Get $1000 credit to start . Tiger Data (creators of TimescaleDB) sponsor EmDash 1.0: An Open Source CMS for Astro — Cloudflare's alternative to WordPress, first announced in April, has reached 1.0. Each site ships with an MCP server, meaning you can set an agent to work out of the box. To accompany the launch, plugins can now be submitted to its registry . Matt Kane How Anthropic Made Claude's Web App Faster — The tale of how a recent sprint (with Claude doing much of the work) cut Claude's time-to-typeable at the 75th percentile from 3.1s to 0.55s, from tracking layout shifts too small for CLS to flag, to a :root:has() selector costing 24ms per DOM change, and a jump caused by Chrome pre-rendering the page at the wrong height. Wang, Attard, and G (Anthropic) ⚡️ IN BRIEF 🌀 Cloudflare has launched Turnstile Spin , a way to let AI agents set up Turnstile's protection on sites you're building. Cloudflare now also has a new cf CLI client which can work with all of its APIs (unlike Wrangler). 🧭 Safari Technology Preview 253 is out now , adding support for network throttling within the Web Inspector, amongst a huge number of fixes. 🦊 Firefox 157 has a new look , which you can see in action here . 📉 In response to recent chatter around the 'death' of web education , Andy Bell shares a bleak sketch of where things stand. 🟢 Version 31 of developer browser Polypane is out now , adding a new canvas layout, elements panel improvements, and an update to Chromium 155. 🔥 Got something you want to say about HTML? Manuel Matuzović is seeking submissions for this year's HTMHell Advent Calendar . 📙 Articles, Opinions & Tutorials Detect When Elements Overlap with CSS — A neat bit of CSS lateral thinking to detect when two elements get too close or overlap, no JavaScript needed. It combines anchor positioning, style container queries, and scroll-driven animations, using an overflowing 'measure' element as the trigger. Ahmad Shadeed Connection Allowlists: Lock Down Where a Page Can Connect — Chrome 152 adds support for a Connection-Allowlist header to tell the browser which servers a page is allowed to talk to (and block everything else). Benz & Zapata (Chrome for Developers) The Future of Frontend Is Agentic: Free OpenAI Course — Join OpenAI's Katia Gil Guzman and learn how to direct Codex through landing pages, dashboards, 3D interfaces, and shipping into an existing codebase. Ollie Williams Extracting Grid Information Using CSS — A neat CSS-only proof of concept technique where you can get information about a grid structure (number of columns/rows, where items sit on the grid, etc). The technique relies on scroll-driven animations, oddly enough. Temani Afif The Interface Cheat Sheet — A helpful illustrated list of good UI advice, touching on points from border radiuses and transitions to the use of color, scaling and accessibility. Jakub Krehel The Era of Agentic Mobile Development Is Built on Expo — Build with our CLI and dev tools. Test on our cloud simulators. And ship with the best CI/CD for mobile development. Expo sponsor Custom Attributes Polyfill — A polyfill for the proposed Custom Attributes spec, letting you attach reusable behaviours to any element via custom attributes with their own lifecycle hooks. Keith Cirkel Fluid Typography — Donnie argues that because container widths are unpredictable, using container queries to drive fluid font sizing isn't the right choice. He suggests we stick with viewport units to retain true control. Donnie D’Amato Stop Buttons Triggering Zoom When They’re Double Tapped Andy Bell Stop Treating CSS Container Queries Like Traditional Media Queries Victor Ayomipo Component Testing: A Practical Guide for Frontend Developers Storybook Blog 🧰 Tools, Code & Resources Transitions.dev: Essential UI Transitions for Web Apps — The home page shows a series of cards, each of which displays a CSS-based UI animation. Drop in your logo, choose which colors should glow, and get an HDR version ready to download. Claims to make things up to 7.5x brighter in Chrome and Safari.
